chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ نَهِيك، السَّمُرِّي، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، الْمُلَقَّبُ " دَحْمَان ".

translations.en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Nahik, al-Samari, Abu Muhammad, the one with the laqab of "Daḥman".
Weak, a proponent of irtifa' in doctrine.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* assesses Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Nahik, known as 'Dahman,' as a weak narrator whose theological elevation of the Imams (*irtifa' al-qawl*) may have contributed to his perceived deficiency in precision. His designation highlights the nuanced criteria used by Shia scholars to distinguish between mere weakness in transmission and specific doctrinal or character traits affecting reliability.
en.seo_question: Who is Abd al-Rahman ibn Nahik and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (in terms of hadith narrator reliability)
key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of Irtifa' (a theological doctrine regarding the Imams' status)
